Visual Design.assessment:
# Cycle 48 independent Visual Design Reviewer

**APPROVE.** The mobile Explorer reads as a single opaque navigation surface from the left viewport edge to the right. In the previous production-matched preview, archive dividers and tiny fragments of text were visible in the exposed strips beside the drawer, especially after folding Blog. The candidate covers them in both themes.

## Inspection

I opened the runnable production-matched baseline on port 48043 and candidate on port 48044 in branded Google Chrome. I inspected Blog’s resting state, open and folded tree, keyboard focus, reduced-motion opening, closing, and opening after scrolling, plus Home, the local graph, the Azure Machine Configuration article and its PowerShell block, search results for Azure, and expanded and collapsed navigation. I used 390 × 844, 900 × 900 and 1440 × 900 in light and pure-black dark mode and reviewed the paired screenshots of those pages, the Certifications archive and the halfway drawer transition. Separate candidate sessions exercised Home, Certifications, the Azure tag and the long-titled Microsoft Defender for Identity article on 320 × 568, 390 × 844, 667 × 375 and 800 × 550. The nested Projects branch was also exercised at those widths in both themes.

- [Paired light mobile evidence](/home/husenjan/Documents/Blog/quartz/design-evidence/explorer-mobile/explorer-390-light.webp) and [dark mobile evidence](/home/husenjan/Documents/Blog/quartz/design-evidence/explorer-mobile/explorer-390-dark.webp).
- The paired context sheets are in [explorer-mobile](/home/husenjan/Documents/Blog/quartz/design-evidence/explorer-mobile/). Additional local Chrome captures and geometry are in [/tmp/quartz-explorer-48/visual](/tmp/quartz-explorer-48/visual).

## Findings

- The candidate increases the 390px tree width from 323px to 358px, retaining 16px outer insets. The rule and selected folder now start at the same visual edge as the close control. “Setting Up Azure Machine Configuration” and “Increasing Disk Space on Linux Servers” each fit on a single line. Long titles use full words and continue onto consistently indented lines. The extra room shows another whole entry in the opening view.
- SN Pro folder labels remain visibly stronger than file entries. The filled selected row distinguishes the current folder or article. Guides meet their chevrons, and 26px between adjacent guide levels communicates nesting. At 320px, the deepest file link occupies about 235px and “Windows Kernel Programming Fundamentals” wraps to three readable lines. The Explorer title, horizontal rule and 44 × 44px close button stay in place when the list scrolls. One-line file entries are 44px high with a 4px gap.
- Colors follow the established warm off-white and black page surfaces. Full-opacity secondary file text remains readable in both palettes. The drawer has no shadow. Its opaque fill covers the surrounding page all the way through the wide empty area under a folded tree. During the normal slide, the portion of the archive still outside the leading edge is briefly visible as expected. Reduced motion sets the transition duration to zero.
- Starting 1,500px into the long article, a direct touchscreen tap opened the panel in place. Closing returned to the same scroll position. Within the expanded Projects folders I scrolled to the final nested link, read the entire title and tapped it to reach the correct article at all four mobile widths and in both themes. Each tree fit its available width. Tab outlines the focused row, and Escape returns focus to the Explorer control.
- Source Serif headlines, TX-02 code, listing rows and search previews retain their typography and measure. The 900px and 1440px sidebar collapse controls and graph remain distinct from the reading column. The graph renders with the expected inks and theme surface. The position adjustment occupies one declaration in the existing mobile component rule and adds no duplication or new design tokens.

I found no remaining visual defect on the inspected pages, and no critical or material regression. Three-line titles in the narrowest nested branch preserve their full wording and existing hierarchy. I recommend no additional stylistic change for this cycle.

Responsive and Accessibility.assessment:
# Cycle 48 · Responsive and Accessibility Reviewer

**APPROVE.** I reproduced the exposed underlying archive in the production-matched baseline. The candidate covers the available mobile viewport in the expanded and folded states. I found no critical, material or minor regression in the tested interactions.

## Change and evidence

I reviewed the one added mobile `position: fixed` declaration in `quartz/styles/custom.scss`, visited the running production-matched previews on ports 48043 and 48044, and checked the local package on ports 48041 and 48042. I inspected the paired opening, expanded, folded, closed and edge-detail screenshots, along with all six light and dark context sheets in `design-evidence/explorer-mobile`. The same article, folder state, typography and viewports were used for each pair.

At 390 × 844, the baseline drawer began 17.55 CSS px inside the left edge. Its opaque area was about 355 px wide. In Chrome, Brave and Linux WebKit the candidate began at (0, 0) and covered 390 × 844. The list grew from about 323 to 358 px while retaining 16 px inner gutters. Both edge hit tests resolved to the drawer. In the produced matched pairs the underlay altered 190 light pixels and 198 dark pixels in the baseline, and zero pixels in the open and folded candidate captures. The visible archive during the opening animation is confined to the area ahead of the moving drawer edge.

## Interaction and readability

- I opened the drawer on Home, Blog, Certifications, Projects, Tags and the Azure Machine Configuration article. From an article scrolled to 1,510 px, a physical-coordinate touch opened the drawer. Escape returned focus to its toggle at the same article position. I followed the drawer link to Increasing Disk Space on Linux Servers and used Back to return to the Azure article. Both navigations left the content interactive and the drawer closed.
- At the default phone text size the toggle and folder disclosure targets measured 44 × 44 CSS px. Visible link and control targets were at least 44 px high. At 320 px with 200% text they were at least 48 px high. The longest visible Blog title wrapped across the available width with matching scroll and client widths at both sizes.
- A Chrome and Brave synthetic finger swipe advanced the tree 289 px while the page stayed still. Reverse Tab from the toggle exposed and focused the final Projects link. The next Tab returned to the toggle. A forward Tab reached the first folder disclosure with a 2 px solid focus ring. Space folded Blog. Chrome's native accessibility tree removed the archive heading on opening, removed the article links on folding Blog, and restored the archive after Escape. Escape restored the toggle and released the inert page. Linux WebKit also scrolled the tree and passed the keyboard sequence. At 800 × 360 the tree scrolled beneath the close control. At 801 px the sidebar used the desktop disclosure.
- At 320 × 568 with 200% text the list had 256 px of usable width and no horizontal overflow. In native Firefox 159 I used 200% and 400% full-page zoom from a 1280 px window in both themes. The drawer filled Firefox's available content width at both scales. At 400% the final Projects row could be brought fully into the 320 × 204 CSS-pixel viewport.
- Chrome’s simulated 33 px left, 27 px right and 24 px bottom safe-area insets were respected. Reduced motion removed the drawer transition. In forced colors the current Blog link had a system-color underline, and keyboard focus retained its own outline.
- Navigation uses 15 px SN Pro in both themes. Ordinary link contrast measured 6.26:1 light and 9.14:1 dark. Current-row text against the selected fill measured 7.06:1 and 11.91:1. The drawer fills were warm off-white and pure black. Code in the matched article retained TX-02 at 14.5 px.
- On the live 390, 900 and 1440 px builds in both themes I tested the Blog and Certifications archives, Home, the Azure article and code block, keyboard Azure search selection, and narrow or wide navigation controls. Home's graph was absent on the phone and rendered a canvas at 900 and 1440 px. The wide sidebar collapsed and reopened by keyboard. The wide archive, search and code pairs retained their layout. The graph continued to simulate on the wider layouts.
- Maintenance scope is one declaration on the existing mobile drawer rule. The change uses existing Quartz background, interaction, scroll-lock and motion rules. It adds no new font, color, animation, event handler or dependency.

The confirmed baseline defect was the side strips exposing inactive page content. The candidate resolves it. No further visual preference or corrective change is required. Browser touch and safe-area coverage used emulation. WebKit was the Linux port. Evidence from this review is in `access-{chrome,brave,webkit}.json`, `access-nativezoom.json` `access-flows.json` and `access-nativeax.json` alongside this report.

CSS and Quartz V5.assessment:
# Independent CSS and Quartz V5 review, cycle 48

**Decision — APPROVE.** The published mobile Explorer now fills the viewport on every tested page. The layout above the mobile breakpoint and the local Quartz component both keep their previous geometry. I found no critical, material or minor stylesheet defect in the change.

**Source and cascade.** The only change in the compiled site stylesheet is the 15 bytes of `position:fixed;` in the existing unlayered `.explorer .explorer-content` rule under Quartz’s inclusive `max-width:800px` query. The component declares that same selector inside `@layer quartz-base`. The published component sets absolute positioning, which anchors it to the narrower sticky sidebar. The local component already sets fixed positioning. The unlayered owner rule applies to both without a specificity increase, duplication of a rule, a new selector, changes to JavaScript or dependency patches. The existing logical insets, safe-area padding, scroll container, height, transform, visibility and stacking order continue to control the drawer. In the paired published preview, all 160 HTML documents containing the Explorer include the published component and the appropriate site stylesheet.

**Pages, viewports and evidence.** I inspected the eight screenshot sheets and compared raw frames. I then opened both published-asset previews in Google Chrome at 390×844, 900×900 and 1440×900 in light and dark themes. I tested Home, Blog, the Certifications archive, the Azure tag listing, the Azure Machine Configuration article and its first fenced block, Search with the Azure query and a keyboard-selected result, and the Home graph on tablet and desktop. At 390px I opened the drawer on each page, including after scrolling the article to its code, and tested folder collapse, Escape, and selecting the Azure article from the Blog drawer. I tested both local-component previews at 390×844 in both themes. Short coarse-pointer landscape checks covered 800×420, 801×390 and 915×412 in both themes on both published previews. I also opened and closed the candidate drawer with reduced motion enabled. Per-state measurements are in `css-review.json` and route transition results in `css-navigation.json` beside this report.

**Visual result, type and themes.** At 390px the published drawer grew from 354.91px wide at x=17.55 to the full 390px at x=0. The candidate list starts 16px inside the viewport. Expanded and folded views have an opaque surface, warm #faf9f5 or pure black. Comparing those frames with a matched version with the Blog content hidden found 190 exposed pixels in the light baseline and 198 in dark. Both candidate comparisons were identical down to the pixel. The nav files retained 15px SN Pro at weight 450, the folders 15px at 550 and both used 21px line height. The article code retained 14.5px TX-02 and 22px line height. The Home graph rendered with the existing #817d72 and #707070 edge tokens.

**Responsive and interaction behavior.** At 800×420 the patch covers the entire viewport, correcting a 688px baseline panel. At 801×390 and 915×412 the desktop toggle operates the in-flow static rail, including on a touch screen. The two wider landscape geometries matched across builds, as did the 900px and 1440px rails. The candidate covered the article at a page scroll offset of 1164px, returned focus to the mobile toggle on Escape and cleared the background’s inert state after navigation. The transform and visibility transitions still use 0.2s with ordinary motion and report 0s with reduced motion. The local builds measured the same 390×844 drawer before and after.

**Build checks.** The production build emitted 913 files. The recorded test log shows 167 passes and zero failures. The separate repository-wide type check reports the same two dependency declaration errors for micromorph and remark-parse/lib in baseline and candidate. My browser measurements cover desktop Chrome’s touch emulation.

Design Director.assessment:
# Cycle 48 independent Design Director decision

**APPROVE.** Accept the one-line mobile Explorer fix in `quartz/styles/custom.scss`. The prior drawer exposed the archive on both sides. The candidate covers the viewport in both themes and gives the navigation tree back the width previously lost to those strips.

## Independent inspection

I ran branded Google Chrome against the previous and candidate sites with the published Explorer assets. I compared the Blog drawer expanded, folded and closed, opened Search and selected an Azure result with the keyboard, and opened the drawer on Home, the Azure tag and the Azure Machine Configuration article. I exercised both themes at 390 × 844 and the dark theme at 800 × 420. On the article, I tapped the toolbar at a page offset of 1,200 CSS px, scrolled the open tree by 300 px and pressed Escape. The article kept its reading position throughout, the close control stayed visible, and focus returned to the toggle. I also inspected the candidate Home graph, sidebar disclosure, Certifications archive and article code at 900 × 900 dark and 1440 × 900 light. Both local-package versions already filled the 390 × 844 viewport. I examined the eight paired evidence sheets, including the normal-motion slide and enlarged folded edges. Screenshots and browser measurements from my own sessions are in the neighboring `director/` directory.

At 390px the published baseline bounds were x=17.55 to x=372.45 and the tree measured 323px wide. The candidate covered x=0 to x=390 and gave its tree 358px. At 800px the prior drawer was 688px wide and the new drawer reached both viewport edges. On each tested mobile page all six left and right sampled points hit the candidate drawer. With Blog folded, the surrounding blank space was opaque to the bottom edge. Expanded titles wrapped cleanly within their nesting level and the current row and folder disclosures remained legible. The drawer used the established off-white and pure-black surfaces. The desktop examples retained the editorial hierarchy, TX-02 code face and distinct graph inks.

## Independent assessments

| Reviewer | Decision | Finding considered |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Visual Design | APPROVE | Open and folded trees cover the archive in both themes. The reclaimed width reduces wrapping. Long titles and the deepest Projects branch stay readable at 320px. |
| Responsive and Accessibility | APPROVE | Touch scrolling, keyboard containment, Escape, forced colors, simulated insets, reduced motion and Firefox full-page zoom worked. The navigation text and selected rows meet their measured contrast thresholds. |
| CSS and Quartz V5 | APPROVE | One unlayered declaration selects the correct containing block within the existing inclusive mobile query. The locally installed Explorer already uses fixed positioning. The static rail above 800px retains its geometry. |

The three assessments agree. The confirmed material defect belongs to the baseline. The candidate resolves it, and I found no material regression or preference requiring a further styling cycle.

## Verification and scope

- All 160 pages containing Explorer passed each theme in Google Chrome and Brave at 390 × 844. Each browser completed 320 distinct route/theme cases. All had full bounds, edge hits, an inert background and restored focus after Escape. The settled Chrome screenshot remained pixel-identical after hiding the background in all 320 cases. The separate Blog edge comparisons had zero candidate differences in Chrome, Brave and Linux WebKit in all 24 width/theme/scroll combinations. The build also contains 91 redirects and a 404 document without Explorer.
- I checked the build log and the full unit-test terminal summary. Quartz emitted 913 files and all 167 tests passed. The changed SCSS passed Prettier and whitespace checks. I reran the content integrity comparison across all 252 HTML paths. Text, links, IDs, runtime scripts and WOFF2 assets matched. The compiled site stylesheet added exactly the 15 bytes of the fixed-position declaration.
- The separate repository-wide type/style checker stopped at the same two dependency diagnostics as the baseline, for `micromorph` and `remark-parse/lib`. The two logs matched byte for byte. This fork's Pages workflow requires the Quartz build. The upstream-only type/style CI job is conditional on the upstream repository. The inherited diagnostics remain recorded in the existing backlog.
- The candidate review used locally served published Explorer assets and emulated touch. The WebKit results cover its Linux port, and the Firefox report covers desktop full-page zoom. These results establish local acceptance. Device hardware and post-deployment rendering fall outside the measured evidence.

**Disposition.** The three required assessments, mandatory automated tests, screenshot evidence and independent final review satisfy the design gate. No further stylesheet correction is required.
